building.name: Summit Tower
building.completed_conflict: The city's Modern & Postmodern styles context statement dates this building 1963; the assessor's roll records it as built 1964.
building.architect: Tibor Fesces of Neill Smith Architects

hook: A condominium tower whose 112 apartments are held as 112 separate parcels, on floors 9 through 32.

narrative.lead: 999 Green Street is a condominium tower whose 112 apartments are held as 112 separate parcels — lots 029 through 140 on block 0127 — numbered 901 through 3202: five to a floor from the ninth through the thirty-first, with no thirteenth, and two more on the thirty-second. The roll lists no unit at this address below the ninth floor.

historical_record.description: The Summit, Joseph Eichler's last San Francisco project: a thirty-two-storey luxury tower designed by Tibor Fesces of Neill Smith Architects, with Claude Oakland as interior architect. Its cantilevered floors end in balcony edges rather than structural members and are carried on two concrete piers. Its scale on the crest of Russian Hill was so unpopular that it led to zoning reform limiting the height and bulk of later hilltop development.
A 106-unit building stood on the site.

unknowns: The Modern design context statement dates the Summit to 1963, 1964 and 1965 in three different passages.
